headline: Beach Tags and State Park Entry Systems
reservation: Most Jersey Shore beaches require daily or seasonal 'beach tags' for access during the summer months; these are sold locally by each municipality. State parks like Island Beach require a vehicle entry fee, and capacity limits may apply during peak weekends. Accommodations should be booked months in advance for July and August stays.

days.title: North Shore Music and Victorian Architecture

stops.name: Asbury Park Boardwalk
stops.detail: Walk the historic waterfront to see the Convention Hall and vibrant murals that define this musical hub.

stops.name: Ocean Grove Tent City
stops.detail: Explore the unique Victorian cottages and the Great Auditorium in this historic religious retreat.

days.driving: Walking within towns; 15-minute local drives between hubs
days.note: Parking in Asbury Park uses a metered app system; check signage for zone details.

days.title: Maritime Forests and Barnegat Views

stops.name: Island Beach State Park
stops.detail: Traverse self-guided nature trails through the last remaining undeveloped barrier island dunes in the state.

stops.name: Barnegat Lighthouse State Park
stops.detail: Climb the historic 'Old Barney' for views of the Atlantic and the commercial fishing fleet at Viking Village.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours; traffic on Route 72 can be heavy during peak summer hours
days.note: Island Beach State Park often reaches vehicle capacity by mid-morning on sunny weekends.

days.title: Southern Tip History and Nature

stops.name: Cape May Point State Park
stops.detail: Visit the lighthouse and walk the freshwater marsh boardwalks popular for migratory bird watching.

stops.name: Sunset Beach
stops.detail: Search for 'Cape May Diamonds' near the concrete remains of the SS Atlantus, a WWI-era shipwreck.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; conditions vary on the Garden State Parkway
days.note: Cape May is a National Historic Landmark; many streets are narrow and best explored on foot or by trolley.

intel.title: Seasonal Beach Parking
intel.text: Public lots in towns like Ocean City fill quickly by 10 AM in summer. Many municipalities require the use of mobile payment apps for street parking near the boardwalk.

intel.title: Reliable Coastal Coverage
intel.text: Cellular service is generally excellent throughout the developed shore towns. You may experience slight drops in the interior trails of the Pine Barrens or remote marsh areas.

intel.title: Parkway Service Areas
intel.text: Fuel stations are frequent along the Garden State Parkway, but New Jersey law prohibits self-service. Wait for an attendant to pump your gas at all stations.

intel.title: Summer Weekend Traffic
intel.text: Southbound traffic on Friday afternoons and northbound on Sunday evenings is extreme. Allow double the estimated travel time when using the Parkway during these windows.

intel.title: Local Beach Tags
intel.text: Unlike most states, NJ beaches are often not free; you must purchase a tag from a booth or roving inspector. Prices and requirements vary significantly between adjacent towns.

plan.arrival: Collect your rental at Newark (EWR) and take the Garden State Parkway south; stop in Toms River for major supplies before entering barrier islands.
plan.vehicle: Standard sedans are ideal for shore towns; high-clearance vehicles are not required for paved coastal roads.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset Beach in Cape May for its namesake views over the Delaware Bay.
